argument_macro_structure.premise_explicitness: Moderate — premises are embedded in the prose rather than formally enumerated

argumentative_quality.dialectical_reasonableness: High — the text presents a genuine paradox and a nuanced resolution that avoids both horns of the dilemma
argumentative_quality.logical_relevance: High — each paragraph builds directly on the previous one, maintaining tight logical continuity
argumentative_quality.premise_acceptability: Moderate — the premises rely on Kantian assumptions about universal cognitive structures that are contestable

explicit_definitions_given: Disinterest — satisfaction independent of concern for the object's existence
Free play — harmonious relationship between imagination and understanding
Formal purposiveness — form that seems designed for our cognitive faculties without a determinate purpose

dialectical_engagement.objection_handling: The text anticipates the objection from conflicting aesthetic judgments and addresses it by distinguishing psychological disagreement from normative claims
objections_raised: Empirical fact of conflicting aesthetic judgments appears to refute universal validity

epistemic_stance_and_voice.certainty_language_frequency: Moderate — uses definitive statements ('is', 'must', 'cannot') but within a Kantian framework presented as exposition

philosophical_orientation.grounding: Transcendental idealism — locating universal validity in the structure of cognition itself
philosophical_orientation.sentiment: Analytic and expository — presenting Kant's position with clarity rather than arguing polemically
philosophical_orientation.thematic_focus: Aesthetics, epistemology of judgment, normativity of taste

structural_organization.structure_type: Progressive elaboration — each paragraph restates and extends the previous one, creating a spiral of increasing specificity

summary_of_core_decisions: The text presents Kant's resolution of the antinomy of taste by relocating the ground of aesthetic judgment from the object to the universal cognitive apparatus, specifically through the twin concepts of disinterest and free play. It systematically distinguishes aesthetic judgments from both merely subjective (agreeable) and purely objective (good) judgments, then resolves the apparent contradiction by positing an indeterminate concept — the supersensible substrate — as the basis for universal communicability.

thesis_commitment.conclusion_type: Synthetic resolution — the paradox is resolved by reconceiving the terms rather than choosing one side
thesis_commitment.hedging_density_in_final_paragraph: Low — the conclusion is stated with confidence as Kant's established position
